A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WebClipper. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations, training-strategy comparisons, and component ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: The original evaluations remain, and Appendix C.1 adds WebExplorer-8B fine-tuning results in Table 3.

M1.justification: Graph construction, pruning, majority voting, selective rewriting, perplexity-based selection, and efficiency/hybrid training remain unchanged. The added approximation wording and WebExplorer-8B experiment do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Training data sources and the four evaluation benchmarks—xbench-deepsearch, Browsecomp, GAIA, and HLE—are retained. The new WebExplorer-8B experiment uses existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 removes DeepSeek-R1-671B from Table 1 across all four benchmarks and from the baseline description. Other main comparators remain; WebExplorer is relabeled WebExplorer-8B rather than replaced.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 adds fine-tuning and evaluation of WebExplorer-8B alongside the existing Tongyi-DeepResearch setting. Previously reported benchmark subsets, evaluation metrics, o3-mini judge, and 100-round budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a model-generalization check: whether WebClipper benefits another base agent, WebExplorer-8B. Existing component ablations, training-strategy analyses, and both empirical case studies are retained. The new Nobel Prize example illustrates rewriting rather than reporting another empirical case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report three evaluation runs with different random seeds and averaged performance in Section 4.1. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures appear.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports fine-tuned WebExplorer-8B results: GAIA accuracy is 0.407 with 8.22 rounds versus its baseline's 0.372 and 12.88; Browsecomp accuracy is slightly lower, 0.135 versus 0.137. DeepSeek results are removed, while other matched results remain unchanged. Table 3 introduces a conflicting GAIA baseline F-AE value, 0.512 versus 0.521 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Graph definitions, costs, Algorithm 1, and the F-AE formulation and derivation remain substantively unchanged. Sampling-index and information-node-index edits are notational corrections. V1 already described MNDAG extraction as approximate in Section 3.4 and Appendix B.3.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly qualifies the mined MNDAG as approximate, narrowing its previously unqualified formulation. The main contributions and claims of roughly 20% efficiency gains with maintained or improved accuracy remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 newly interprets the WebExplorer-8B results as evidence of applicability beyond one model. Expanded Appendix B.4 explains how references to deleted observations can encourage hallucinated observations during training. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract and discloses that extraction and rewriting use eight H800 80GB GPUs and can finish within one day. These are newly documented resource details; the existing fine-tuning settings and prompt descriptions remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Xiong et al. (2026), Scaling Search-Augmented LLM Reasoning via Adaptive Information Control, to the introduction and references. The related-work narrative otherwise remains unchanged; the DeepSeek-R1 reference survives despite removal of its benchmark comparison.

P1.justification: V2 expands Appendix B.4 with a worked rewriting example and reorganizes Appendix C into Additional Experiment Results, with the existing cases nested under C.2. Local wording, notation, and corresponding-author details also change, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 3, removes DeepSeek rows from Table 1, and adjusts Table 2 spacing. Existing case-study tables become Tables 4–5 and move with appendix reflow. Figures and their substantive content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The second-agent experiment adds useful evidence beyond Tongyi-DeepResearch, while the rewriting example and compute/code disclosures improve clarity and reproducibility information. These provide a modest net benefit despite the removed DeepSeek comparison and the new GAIA F-AE inconsistency between Tables 1 and 3. The core method and existing results remain stable.
